articles.headline: Kick It Out: Discrimination 'deeply embedded' in football, reports up 25%
articles.description: Discrimination remains "deeply embedded" in English football, the chief executive of Kick It Out has said, with reports up 25%  last season compared to the prior campaign.

articles.headline: Ex-Arsenal midfielder Aaron Ramsey named Oxford United manager
articles.description: Aaron Ramsey has stepped into management by taking the reins at Oxford United.

articles.headline: Notts County beat David Beckham's Salford in League Two playoff final
articles.description: Sir David Beckham made an unhappy Wembley Stadium return as Notts County beat the Salford side he co-owns 3-0 to win the League Two playoff final.

article.headline: Wrexham concede top spot to Birmingham after goalless draw
article.description: Wrexham slipped to second in the League One table on Saturday after they played out a goalless draw with Leyton Orient in east London,

images.name: Arthur Okonkwo of Wrexham during the Sky Bet League One match between Wrexham AFC and Shrewsbury Town FC  [1296x729]

peers.name: Arthur Okonkwo of Wrexham during the Sky Bet League One match between Wrexham AFC and Shrewsbury Town FC  [1296x1296]
Arthur Okonkwo of Wrexham during the Sky Bet League One match between Wrexham AFC and Shrewsbury Town FC  [1296x729]
Arthur Okonkwo of Wrexham during the Sky Bet League One match between Wrexham AFC and Shrewsbury Town FC  [864x1296]
Arthur Okonkwo of Wrexham during the Sky Bet League One match between Wrexham AFC and Shrewsbury Town FC  [1296x864]
Arthur Okonkwo of Wrexham during the Sky Bet League One match between Wrexham AFC and Shrewsbury Town FC  [1296x518]

article.story:
Wrexham slipped to second in the League One table on Saturday after they played out a goalless draw with Leyton Orient in east London while Birmingham City went top following a dramatic win over Peterborough United.

Goalkeeper Arthur Okonkwo kept his fifth clean sheet of the season in the stalemate as Wrexham struggled to impose themselves on an Orient team that began the day 16th in the table.

Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson opted to select Jack Marriott over Paul Mullin up front, but his team struggled to carry a threat in attacking areas, with their seven shots bettered by Orient's nine on a day when the two teams' respective defences dominated.

The Welsh club, who are co-owned by Hollywood actors Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney, have enjoyed a positive start to their first season in the third tier of English football following their promotion last season, going unbeaten in their first five matches before succumbing to a 3-1 away defeat to Birmingham on Sep. 16.

Birmingham, who count NFL legend Tom Brady among their investors, spent lavishly in the summer transfer window in order to acquire a calibre of player who they felt could get them promoted back to the Championship at the first time of asking following their relegation last season.

The supposed rivalry between the two clubs was stoked ahead of their meeting at St. Andrews when Wrexham drafted in Eli Manning as a fan. Manning beat Brady's New England Patriots in two Super Bowls as quarterback of the New York Giants.

Brady responded with a well-mannered boast about his own Super Bowl successes.

Wrexham travel to face Stevenage in their next League One fixture on Tuesday.
